full_judgment: 11. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has taken us through the order sheet of the trial Court. It appears that the petitioner was allowed bail by the learned Magistrate and after submission of charge-sheet while the records were transmitted to the Special Tribunal for trial he was along on bail and attended the Court till 31-5-1998. He was found absent on the following day ie 21-6-98, so his lawyer filed an application for time and on the next day ie 8-7-1998, due to his absence his bail was cancelled and the Tribunal proceeded under section 339 B of the Code of Criminal Procedure without any further steps to secure has attendance nor his sureties were asked to produce him. The Tribunal was, of course, required to follow section 27(6A) of the Special Powers Act in such case. He was subsequently convicted on 20-7-1998 by the impugned judgment. In paragraph 10 of his application the petitioner stated that on 18-7-1998 he was attacked by brain hemorrhage and in consequence his entire body was paralyzed and he could not move and thereafter it was not possible on his part to appear before the Court physically. Ultimately, he became dumb and he lost strength to move and he was bed-ridden and expecting the touch of icy hands of death. Though he was still alive but he was unable to move and that in the meantime Judgment was pronounced on 20-7-1998 which he could not know due to his incurable disease and that being unaware of the date of pronouncement of the judgment he could not do anything. And the police arrested him on 20-6-2001 and produced him before the court on 21-6-2001 and the learned Court sent him to the jail for suffering imprisonment. But in the meantime the period of limitation for preferring appeal under section 30 of the Act was over and under the circumstances finding no other alternative relief or reliefs provided in any other law but to file the present writ petition under Article 102 of the Constitution the petitioner filed the instant petition. On consideration of the facts and circumstances and the statement made by the petitioner we are of the view that the petitioner thus made out a case preventing him from availing of the alternative remedy.
